Design is unpaired, single batch, 6 treated vs 6 control, sex and age not matched between arms.
steps.question: Are the 12000 x 13 raw Salmon counts and the 12-sample metadata (condition, sex, age) internally consistent, and how imbalanced are sex and age between the 6 treated and 6 control adipose samples?
constraints: Do not drop any sample without explicit justification reported in output
Use raw integer counts as-is; do not normalize at this step (normalization belongs to the DE step)
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in counts.csv columns match metadata.csv rows exactly (n=12 after excluding gene symbol column)
Report per-group counts of sex (F/M) and summary stats (mean, sd, range) of age for treated vs control
Report library size per sample and number of genes with near-zero counts across all samples
Low-count gene filter applied and documented (e.g., minimum count threshold) prior to DE
Explicit statement of the direction and magnitude of the age imbalance between groups, since design is unpaired and unmatched

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, condition adjusted for sex and age vs unadjusted
caveats: With only 6 vs 6 samples and 2 additional covariates (sex, age), degrees of freedom are limited; do not add further covariates or interaction terms without strong justification

Age as continuous covariate assumes roughly linear effect on expression across the observed range; verify age range reported in T1S1 is wide enough that this is a reasonable assumption, and note it as an assumption in output either way
steps.context: 12000 x 12 filtered raw count matrix and metadata with condition (treated/control), sex (F/M), age (years) from T1S1. Adipose tissue, human, single batch, unpaired 6 vs 6 design with unmatched age between groups — the core reason this step must include sex+age as covariates rather than a simple two-group test.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control adipose samples when the model adjusts for sex and age as covariates (design ~ sex + age + condition), and how does this gene list compare to an unadjusted design (~ condition) given the groups are not age-matched?
constraints: Use raw integer counts as DESeq2 input (do not pre-normalize)
condition must be the last term in the adjusted design formula so it is the tested contrast
Report both adjusted and unadjusted results — do not report only one model
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run on raw integer counts filtered in T1S1, using design ~ sex + age + condition with condition as the primary contrast (treated vs control)
A second DESeq2 run using design ~ condition only, for direct comparison
Output table per gene: log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, for both models
Report overlap and discordance between adjusted and unadjusted significant gene sets (padj < 0.05) with counts

Report number of genes reaching padj < 0.05 in the adjusted model, and flag if age or sex itself associates significantly with expression across many genes (i.e., covariates are doing real work, not just diluting power)
Given n=6 per group, explicitly note the limited power to detect small effect sizes and interaction effects

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on covariate-adjusted DE genes
caveats: Pathway enrichment on a small n=6-per-group DE list may yield few or no significant pathways; report a null result plainly rather than lowering thresholds to manufacture a hit
steps.context: DESeq2 adjusted-model results table (gene symbol, log2FoldChange, padj) from T1S2 for human adipose treated vs control comparison. Reference pathway gene sets: WikiPathways human (HGNC gene symbols) available at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes significantly differentially expressed between treated and control adipose samples in the sex/age-adjusted DESeq2 model?
constraints: Match gene identifiers by HGNC symbol as given in counts.csv; do not attempt ID conversion unless a mismatch is detected
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run separately on up- and down-regulated significant genes (padj < 0.05) from the adjusted model in T1S2
Uses WikiPathways human gene sets matched to HGNC gene symbols (same identifier space as the counts.csv gene symbol column)
Report enriched pathways with adjusted p-value (e.g., FDR < 0.05) and the overlapping gene list per pathway

If fewer than 10 significant DE genes are available, report this explicitly and run enrichment on the ranked full gene list (e.g., GSEA-style) instead of over-representation analysis, rather than silently failing

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusting for age/sex
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 adipose samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, with sex and age recorded but not matched between groups. Age and sex are known confounders of adipose gene expression, and imbalance between arms (unmatched age) risks confounding the treatment effect if not modeled explicitly. The plan: (1) load raw Salmon gene counts and metadata, QC the count matrix (library size, filtering low-count genes) and check for age/sex imbalance between treated and control groups; (2) run DESeq2 differential expression with a design that includes condition + sex + age as covariates, so the treatment effect is estimated adjusting for these confounders, and additionally report the unadjusted condition-only model for comparison to show how much the covariates change the result; (3) run pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human) on the covariate-adjusted DE gene list to give biological context to the significant genes. This directly answers 'which genes differ between treated and control' while explicitly accounting for the stated sex/age imbalance rather than ignoring it.
